notes.trap: The result is BINARY, not STRING, even though the documented examples print readable text. Wrap the call in `cast(...)` AS STRING before comparing it with strings. The documented key sizes of 16, 24 and 32 are bytes, not bits.

The default mode is GCM. With no IV, a random 12-byte IV is generated and prepended to the output, so results are non-deterministic and longer than the input: 12-byte IV + ciphertext + 16-byte tag. Only ECB, or an explicit IV, gives repeatable output.
On success it returns NULL (type void), not true. A NULL argument counts as 'not true' and throws.
Positive values are 1-based within 32768-bit buckets: position is (value - 1) % 32768. So 1 and 32769 both map to bit 0, and 0 also maps to bit 0. Always pair it with `bitmap_bucket_number(...)`.
Buckets for positive values start at 1, not 0: bucket is (value - 1) / 32768 + 1. So 32768 is still bucket 1, 32769 is bucket 2, and 0 is bucket 0.
Unlike `=`, it never returns NULL: two NULLs compare as true, and one NULL gives false. It behaves the same as the `<=>` operator.
By default, allowDifferentLgConfigK is false. Merging sketches built with different lgConfigK values fails at runtime instead of downsampling; pass true as the third argument to allow it.

notes.trap: When no file is being read (literals, VALUES, or after shuffles), it returns an empty string, not NULL. Checks with `isnull(...)` therefore never fire.
The result is always STRING (String.valueOf of the Java return value), whatever the Java method returns. Only static methods can be called, and argument types must exactly match a Java overload.

Its return type is NULL (void), so it fits in any CASE or `if(...)` branch. It only throws if that branch is actually evaluated. In 3.5 the error is a plain java.lang.RuntimeException carrying the message.

notes.trap: A wrong key or corrupted input returns NULL instead of an error. This can silently hide key mistakes; `aes_decrypt(...)` would raise an error instead.
